title: NTC Thermistors for Shelf Temperature Control in Food Freeze-Drying: An Alternative to Thermocouples
content: Precise shelf temperature control during freeze-drying is essential for product quality, with thermocouples being the most traditionally used sensors in shelf temperature control systems. This paper evaluates NTC thermistors as alternative temperature sensors for shelf temperature control in freeze-drying processes. A thermistor-based measurement system (accuracy of ±0.17 °C) was integrated into a freeze-dryer. Discretized PI controllers were designed for three independent shelves, evaluated through computational simulations, and implemented on an ESP32 platform. Experimental validation was conducted during freeze-drying of onion (Allium cepa) under vacuum (1 mbar) at a +10 °C setpoint. The implemented system achieved a steady-state error below 0.3 °C and effectively rejected disturbances during primary drying. An overshoot below 2% was observed. The solution proved to be simple, low-cost, and accurate for shelf temperature control in food freeze-drying processes using NTC thermistors as sensors, thus serving as an alternative to traditional thermocouples in this type of process. Future studies may implement adaptive controllers and expand the temperature control range.
